title.narrative: First Competitive and Inclusive Tajikistan DPO

description.narrative: The Program Development Objective is to support the authorities in their efforts to (a) further open the economy to competition and create favorable market conditions for private sector development; and (b) strengthen the efficiency, transparency, and accountability of the public sector for better services delivery.

The objectives of the First Competitive and Inclusive Tajikistan Development Policy Operation Program for Tajikistan is to support the authorities in their efforts to (a) further open the economy to competition and create favorable market conditions for private sector development; and (b) strengthen the efficiency, transparency, and accountability of the public sector for better service delivery. This first DPO (DPO1) consists of a 50 million dollar International Development Association (IDA) grant. It follows the successful reengagement operation in 2023, the Resilient and Sustainable Tajikistan DPO, reflecting the authorities continued demand for World Bank Group (WBG) support to advance structural reforms for economic growth and closely aligned with WBG's support for Rogun Hydropower Plant (HPP). The Rogun HPP is a transformational large project that will become the main pillar of Tajikistan's electricity system and has a significant potential to contribute to decarbonization of electricity systems of Central Asian countries. The new DPO series supports the implementation of Tajikistan's National Development Strategy 2030 and is aligned with the Country Partnership Framework (CPF). The DPO series also supports reforms to strengthen public services delivery and to create a more inclusive economy. Specifically, it supports: further strengthening of the TSA program by improving its coverage and introducing activation mechanisms for the unemployed; implementation of a new rule-based formula to allocate subnational resources for education to ensure more adequate and equitable resourcing; commencement of reporting on budgetary resources received by frontline health and education service delivery units; and introduction of transparency in the use of public resources from revenues from the Rogun HPP, maximizing the developmental impact of the project through the establishment of a Benefits Sharing Program to use part of the revenues from electricity sales to increase pro-poor spending.

title.narrative: Increased effectiveness of the implementation of ICAO standards and recommended practices as measured by a % score obtained in ICAO Universal Safety Audit

comment.narrative: While an updated audit score is not yet available, this RI#2(b) is in principle on track based on implementation progress. In February 2026, the ICAO conducted a preliminary off-site safety audit and is planning to do a full on-site audit before the end of 2026. The early result of the virtual off-site assessment is close to 90% effective implementation of the protocol questions that have been audited (25% of the total). The final % score from the ICAO Universal Safety Audit will be known in early 2027.

Improved cost recovery in the power sector as measured by technical and commercial losses in transmission and distribution

comment.narrative: The sector is well on track to meet the RI#7(a) targets set for 2027: - Transmission losses went down from 3.5% in 2022 to 3.3% in 2024 and 3.1% in 2025 (reaching the 2027 target of 3.1% ahead of time) - Distribution losses went down from 25.0% in 2022 to 19.23 in 2024 and 15.6% in 2025 (in May 2026, the DPO2 ROC meeting approved changing the 2027 target from 22% to 15%)

Increased Internet affordability as measured by an average cost of 1GB of mobile data priced in US$, at a retail level

comment.narrative:
This RI#1(a) is on track. Since data by bestbroadbanddeals.co.uk has not been updated since 2023, the team referred to other public sources to trace progress made so far. According to data collected by AsiaPlus from four mobile operators and based on the DPO team's calculations, average prices for mobile internet decreased by about 8% (weighted average) in 2025, compared to 2024. Source: https://t.me/asiaplus/96530.
The additional RI#1(b), added at DPO2 ROC stage, is also on track. This RI measures Internet affordability by data-only mobile broadband basket of 5GB as a % share of GNI per capita. According to ITU data, this RI improved from 6.97% in 2023 to 4.99% in 2025 (with a target of 4.00% by end-2027). Source: https://beta.datahub.itu.int/dashboards/ipb/?e=TJK&u=%25 +GNI+per+capita&utm_source=chatgpt.com&i=36056&y=2025

Increased tax revenues (following the reduction of tax and customs incentives) measured as a percentage share of GDP

comment.narrative: This RI#4(a) is on track. According to the Ministry of Finance (MoF), actual tax revenue amounted to TJS 37,466.6 million or 21.2% of GDP in 2025. Apparently, the tax expenditure reforms are paying off. However, there might be some one off elements in 2025 that may not sustain over the medium term. With some VAT rate cuts envisioned, the 2027 target remains realistic.

Increased women's participation in economic decision-making and leadership as measured by the number of women represented in active boards of joint-stock companies with state ownership

comment.narrative:
This RI#6(a) may be off track. The State Investment Committee could not provide the required data upon request, as there is no statistical system created to trace progress with this RI. While it is not known if there is any progress with this RI, the team decided to keep the interim (current) result at the Baseline level for now.
---> To bring this RI back on track, the government may consider adopting a gender quota for SOE boards and require its monitoring by the authorized body though a properly established statistical recording system. Additionally, the State Investment Committee will need to create a pool of professional independent directors that should be consistent with the gender quota suggested.

Higher investor interest as measured by the number of newly registered foreign companies per year, a two-year average

comment.narrative: This RI#3 is in principle on track based on proxy data. The interim result represents a change in the stock of registered foreign companies over two years (2024-2025). According to the tax authority, the number of registered companies with foreign participation is on a rise, from 2,309 companies at end-2023, to 2,666 companies at end-2025 and 2,769 companies at end-2025. While the team was able to obtain this stock data, a breakdown into entering and exiting companies with foreign participation has not been provided by the tax authority yet.

Enhanced transparency of state aid provision as measured by the increase in the number of state aid decisions adopted per year by the Antimonopoly Service following the new procedures and guidelines

comment.narrative:
This RI#4(b) may be off track. Since the adoption of new procedures and guidelines for the endorsement or rejection of state aid measures (the guidelines were adopted in January 2025), the Antimonopoly Service has not received nor considered any applications for state aid. Thus, the new regulations have not been applied yet.
---> To bring this RI back on track, the government is expected to conduct an analysis of the provision of state aid since the beginning of 2025. This analysis will help the Antimonopoly Service to improve the new procedures and guidelines further and to start reviewing applications and making decisions on new state aid measures.

title.narrative: Improved effectiveness of the revised antitrust framework as measured by the increase in the number of anti-competitive practices sanctioned by the Antimonopoly Service

comment.narrative:
This RI#5 is related to a new policy area under DPO2 and will be monitored throughout 2027. The new Competition Law is still with Parliament for approval (expected by fall 2026).
---> To make sure that this RI is achieved by end-2027, when the new Competition Law is endorsed by Parliament, the government will work on a new regulation governing procedures for sanctioning investigations by the Antimonopoly Service.

title.narrative: Increased number of schools that meet the minimum standards for quality of teaching and learning environment under the new framework

comment.narrative:
There is some but limited progress with this RI#10(a). According to the Bank's LEARN project team, two schools were renovated in line with the minimum standards set out in the national education development framework in 2025, and nine more schools are expected to be completed in 2026. Additional schools outside the project framework will also be renovated in line with the framework by other development partners. This information is not yet available and will be reflected in the next reporting cycle.
---> To make sure that this RI meets its target by end-2027, the Ministry of Education has to come up with a proper financing plan covering funding available from the government budget as well as from development partners. The Bank's LEARN team will continue providing advice on this when and where needed.

Increased budget for the targeted social assistance program as measured by its share in total government expenditure, excluding spending on Rogun HPP

comment.narrative: This RI#9 is on track. According to MoF data, actual TSA budget spending amounted to TJS 266.1 million in 2025 which represented a share of 0.57% of total actual budget spending in 2025, excluding actual budget spending on Rogun HPP construction (TJS 8,102 million in 2025). While there are no further plans for increasing the TSA budget, its envelope is anticipated to stay close to the 0.60% target set for 2027.

Ringfenced public funding to the health sector as measured by its share in total government expenditure, excluding spending on Rogun HPP

comment.narrative:
This RI#10(b) is on track. According to MoF data, total actual budget spending on the health sector amounted to TJS 4,364.5 million in 2025 which represented a share of 9.42% of total actual budget spending in 2025, excluding actual budget spending on Rogun HPP construction (TJS 8,102 million in 2025). There are plans to maintain the health budget envelope at above the 9% target.
To complement this RI, there is an additional RI#10(c) suggested and agreed at the ROC stage for DPO2. This new RI is on track. It monitors progress in one of performance indicators of the Public Expenditure and Financial Accountability (PEFA) assessment. Since MoF has already published budget data on resources received by frontline service delivery units in the field of primary healthcare and education, the PEFA score for performance indicator 8.3 can be much higher than 'D' reported in the 2022 PEFA. The new PEFA has been launched and will be finalized by end-2026.

Improved air connectivity as measured by the number of weekly international departing flights from Tajikistan, with temporary exclusions

comment.narrative: This RI#2(a) is well on track and may exceed the initial target set for 2027. According to OAG Aviation data, the number of departing flights from Tajikistan increased from 579 in Q4 2024 to 790 in Q4 2025 (excluding all destinations in Russia). This represents an increase of 36.4% in Q4 2025, compared to Q4 2024, and translates into a weekly average of 60.1 flights (regular and seasonal).

Enabled new renewable energy capacity from private investors as measured in Megawatt of new capacity generated

comment.narrative: This RI#7(b) is on track and may exceed the initial target set for 2027. On 13 January, 2026 an Investment Agreement was signed between the Government of Tajikistan and Ayon Energy LLC for the construction and commissioning of two photovoltaic (PV) solar power plants: a 250 MW facility in the Asht district, Sughd region and a 250 MW facility in the Jayhun district, Khatlon region. Both PV solar power plants are expected for commissioning by end 2026. Total investment of the projects amounts to USD 250 million.

Improved equity in electricity tariff setting as measured by the contribution of the increased tariff for better recovery of electricity system costs of supply to TALCO

comment.narrative:
This RI#8 is progressing slowly but may not meet the ambitious target set for 2027. DPO team's RI calculations are based on data published by the Ministry of Energy and Water Resources. The persistent low payment discipline by TALCO undermines the objective of this reform.
---> To accelerate the implementation of this important reform and make sure that this RI is met, the Board of TALCO, chaired by the Prime Minister, has to come up with a plan of staying current with its electricity bills payments. Otherwise, the government has to step in. The Bank will continue providing TA on this under the Rogun TA project.
